name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightColorIndex.meets
theorem_title: Execution of an index-coloring family member
natural_language_statement:
Let $\lambda,P,d,\mu$ be Light limits, program, depth and memory. Let $W$ be bit width, $m<2^W$ an index, $p$ a coloring parameter selecting two bit coordinates and four colors, and $a$ a correct powers-table base. Suppose $P$ contains the color evaluator and recursive mask-erasure bodies; addresses fit words; the $W+1$ power cells fit memory; $2^{W+1}$ fits a word; and $d+W+1$ is permitted. The evaluator returns

$$\operatorname{color}_p(m)$$

within its prescribed width-dependent time, leaving memory unchanged.

This gives actual execution of each deterministic coloring used to separate three original positions.
explanation: This gives actual execution of each deterministic coloring used to separate three original positions.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightColorParameters.meets
theorem_title: Execution of coloring-parameter decoding
natural_language_statement:
Let $W,t,a\in\mathbb N$ be bit width, coloring index and six-cell destination. Let $\lambda,P,d,\mu$ be limits, program, depth and memory. Suppose the program contains the parameter-decoder and small-division bodies, a nested call is permitted, addresses fit words, $a+6$ fits memory and $t+W+10$ fits a word. The call returns $a$, writes the exact six-field coloring parameter record $\operatorname{data}(W,t)$, uses its specified $t$-dependent time and changes no cell outside those six.

This constructs coloring parameters from a physical index without assuming supplied parameter rows.
explanation: This constructs coloring parameters from a physical index without assuming supplied parameter rows. The six stored fields are decoded by actual integer divisions and can be consumed by the original-index color evaluator.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightDownsetEnumeration.meets
theorem_title: Execution of compact downset enumeration
natural_language_statement:
Let $L,c,a,p,d\in\mathbb N$ be width, cutoff, destination, powers base and depth, with $c\le L$. Suppose the Light program contains the downset wrapper and recursive layer enumerator; memory $\mu$ has the correct $L+1$ powers table; addresses fit words; the powers fit memory and $2^{L+1}$ fits a word. Assume the complete output of capacity $D(L,c)$ ends before the power table and $d+L+1$ is permitted. Then the call returns

$$D(L,c)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}\binom Li,$$

writes the exact ordered compact downset enumeration at $a$, runs within its prescribed budget and preserves every cell outside that capacity.

This constructs the compact mask domain used by stored subset transforms.
explanation: This constructs the compact mask domain used by stored subset transforms. Each cardinality layer appears in the prescribed order, and the returned count is the sum of its binomial sizes.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorLayout.meets
theorem_title: Execution of selected-color normalization layout
natural_language_statement:
Let positive $n,g$ be input length and band size, $a$ an arbitrary free address, and $\lambda,P,d,\mu$ limits, program, depth and memory. Suppose the program contains the layout and division bodies, addresses fit words, the computed normalized-end address plus one fits memory, the stated layout word bound fits, and a nested call is allowed. The layout call writes its normalized-header values at $a$, returns

$$\operatorname{normalizedEnd}(a,n,g),$$

runs within its specified budget and preserves every cell below $a$.

This computes the physical color-normalization buffers from original size and band size.
explanation: This computes the physical color-normalization buffers from original size and band size. The returned normalized-end address and stored pointer header are derived from the two scalar size parameters.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorWantedHeader.meets
theorem_title: Reading the computed wanted-header address
natural_language_statement:
Let $f,h,J,\ell\in\mathbb N$ be cover base, microblock parameter, block count and A-incidence length. Suppose memory $\mu$ satisfies the complete retained cover/key-data contract at $f$. For Light limits, program and depth $\lambda,P,d$, assume the program contains the wanted-header body, addresses fit words and the computed wanted-header address fits memory. Then the call on $(f,J,\ell)$ returns

$$\operatorname{wantedFree}(f,h,J,\ell),$$

within its prescribed $J$-dependent time, leaving all memory unchanged.

This obtains the next physical header from retained construction data rather than external pointer advice.
explanation: This obtains the next physical header from retained construction data rather than external pointer advice.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightHistogram.count_ends
theorem_title: Histogram counting from a zeroed destination
natural_language_statement:
Let $\lambda,P,d$ be run limits, program and depth; $\ell$ a local-variable map; $\mu$ memory; and $s,b,n,p\in\mathbb N$ source, destination, item count and residue count. Assume the first three locals hold $s,b,n$; addresses fit words; both arrays fit memory and are disjoint; source entry $i<n$ holds a natural code $c_i<p$; and every destination cell starts at zero. The counting statement ends within its specified $n$-dependent time with

$$\mu'(b+r)=|\{i<n:c_i=r\}|\qquad(r<p),$$

preserving every cell outside the histogram.

This establishes exact multiplicity counting for physical input and hash-code arrays.
explanation: This establishes exact multiplicity counting for physical input and hash-code arrays. Starting from zero, the program increments once per stored code and preserves every cell outside the histogram.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightLookupSum.meets
theorem_title: Execution of a table-lookup sum
natural_language_statement:
Let $\lambda,P,d,\mu$ be limits, program, depth and memory. Let $a_k,a_t,n,p,B\in\mathbb N$ be key/table bases, key count, table length and entry bound. Suppose procedure $q$ is the lookup-sum body, both arrays fit memory and addresses fit words; the keys equal $c_i<p$, table entries equal $f(r)\le B$, and $nB$ fits a word. The routine returns

$$\sum_{i<n}f(c_i)$$

within its prescribed linear scan budget and leaves memory unchanged.

This charges actual histogram lookups and accumulation in modular counting.
explanation: This charges actual histogram lookups and accumulation in modular counting. The output sums precisely the table entries indexed by the stored key sequence, including repeated keys.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightMinimum.meets
theorem_title: Execution of least-index minimum selection
natural_language_statement:
Let $\lambda,P,d,\mu$ be limits, program, depth and memory. Let $a,n\in\mathbb N$ with $n>0$, and $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$. Suppose procedure $p$ is the minimum body, addresses fit words, the $n$ source cells at $a$ fit memory and store $f(0),\ldots,f(n-1)$. The call returns the least index minimizing $f$ on that range:

$$r=\min\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{i<n}f(i),$$

within its prescribed $n$-dependent time, leaving memory unchanged.

This fixes deterministic first-minimum choices in offset and greedy-selection implementations.
explanation: This fixes deterministic first-minimum choices in offset and greedy-selection implementations. Equal minimum values are resolved by the least physical index, making subsequent algorithmic choices deterministic.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightNatPower.meets
theorem_title: Execution of natural exponentiation
natural_language_statement:
Let $b,e\in\mathbb N$, $\mu$ any integer memory, and $\lambda,P,d$ limits, program and depth. If procedure $p$ is the power body, $e$ fits a word and every $b^i$ for $i\le e$ fits a word, then

$$\operatorname{result}=b^e$$

within its prescribed exponent-dependent time, with the entire memory unchanged.

This realizes the scalar powers needed for finite counts, moduli and representation caps.
explanation: This realizes the scalar powers needed for finite counts, moduli and representation caps. The contract exposes the exponent-dependent step budget and requires every intermediate natural power to fit a word.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightOriginalTripleRow.meets
theorem_title: Execution of one original-position triple test
natural_language_statement:
Let $n>0$, $t<n^3$, $U,a\in\mathbb N$, and $x:\operatorname{Fin}(n)\to\mathbb Z$ with $|x_i|\le U$. Suppose memory $\mu$ stores $x$ at $a$, that segment fits memory, addresses fit words and the explicit triple-row word budget fits. Let a Light program contain the triple-test and small-division bodies, with a nested call allowed at depth $d$. The call returns a Boolean and

$$r=1\iff\operatorname{witness}(x,n,t),$$

where the witness is the distinct-position zero-sum condition for the triple decoded from $t$. It meets the stated row-time bound and leaves memory unchanged.

This supports the exact original-input fallback for the finite exceptional size regime.
explanation: This supports the exact original-input fallback for the finite exceptional size regime. The decoded triple is tested against the original array and all three pairwise index inequalities.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightOutputDecodeDivide.meets
theorem_title: Division through the retained doubling-table routine
natural_language_statement:
Let $a,M,V,f\in\mathbb N$, with $a\le V$, and let $\lambda,P,d,\mu$ be limits, program, depth and memory. Suppose $M,V,f$ satisfy the verified remainder precondition, including positive modulus, sufficient word magnitude and logarithmic scratch space. If the selected procedure is the output-decoding division body, it returns

$$\lfloor a/M\rfloor$$

within the specified division time and preserves every memory cell below $f$.

This performs physical output-index decoding using only the allowed arithmetic and scratch operations.
explanation: This performs physical output-index decoding using only the allowed arithmetic and scratch operations.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightRadixDigit.meets
theorem_title: Execution of radix-digit extraction
natural_language_statement:
Let $k,b,p\in\mathbb N$, $\mu$ an integer memory, and $\lambda,P,d$ limits, program and depth. Suppose the program contains the radix-digit body and small-division helper, a nested call is allowed, and the explicit digit word envelope fits. The call returns

$$\left\lfloor k/b\right\rfloor\bmod p$$

within its stated $k$-dependent time, leaving memory unchanged. Both natural division and remainder use their total conventions, including zero parameters.

This implements exact ordered coefficient and record digit decoding.
explanation: This implements exact ordered coefficient and record digit decoding. The result is the quotient modulo the radix, with the total natural-number conventions retained at zero parameters.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightReportingBucketRow.meets
theorem_title: Counting matching original values through a selected index row
natural_language_statement:
Let $\lambda,P,d,\mu$ be limits, program, depth and memory. Let $N,n,a_v,a_i\in\mathbb N$, target $z\in\mathbb Z$, value map $v:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ and index map $j:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be given. Suppose the program contains the bucket-row body, both source segments fit memory, addresses fit words, $j(i)<N$ for $i<n$, and the arrays store exactly $j(i)$ and $v(k)$. If all $|v(k)|$ for $k<N$ and $|z|$ fit words, it returns

$$|\{i<n:v(j(i))=z\}|$$

within its prescribed scan time, preserving all memory.

This scans only the selected original-index fiber during terminal exact-value checking.
explanation: This scans only the selected original-index fiber during terminal exact-value checking. The test reads the physical index row and returns the exact multiplicity of the target among those original values.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightReportingFilter.meets
theorem_title: Execution of positive-count filtering
natural_language_statement:
Let $n,s,b,d\in\mathbb N$, $c:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, and $\lambda,P,\mu$ be run limits, program and memory. Suppose the filter body is in the program, addresses fit words, disjoint length-$n$ source and destination segments fit memory, and source cell $s+i$ stores $c(i)$ within the word bound for every $i<n$. The procedure writes the ordered selected indices

$$[\,i<n:c(i)>0\,]$$

at $b$, returns their count within its prescribed scan time, and changes no cell outside the length-$n$ destination reservation.

This realizes the positive-frontier selection used by output-sensitive reporting.
explanation: This realizes the positive-frontier selection used by output-sensitive reporting. The ordered output contains exactly the source positions whose stored natural counts are positive.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightScales.meets
theorem_title: Execution of the exact integer microblock scales
natural_language_statement:
Let $n,b,d\in\mathbb N$ and $\mu$ be input length, five-cell destination, depth and memory. Let $\lambda,P$ be limits and a program containing the scale body with its logarithm, rounded cube-root, rounded-half and division helpers at their recorded indices. Suppose addresses fit words, $b+5$ fits memory, $35000000000(n+1)$ fits a word and a nested call is allowed. The procedure writes the exact five scale values, returns

$$\mu(n),$$

runs within its prescribed scale time and preserves every cell outside the five-cell output.

This executes the natural-number schedule underlying the certified runtime exponent.
explanation: This executes the natural-number schedule underlying the certified runtime exponent. The five-cell header is computed by the concrete logarithm, root, halving and division routines.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightSign.meets
theorem_title: Execution of a signed parity factor
natural_language_statement:
Let $e\in\mathbb N$, $x\in\mathbb Z$, $\mu$ an integer memory, and $\lambda,P,d$ limits, program and depth. Suppose the program contains the sign body, addresses fit words, $e$ is within the address-space bound and $|x|$ fits a word. Then the procedure returns

$$(-1)^e x$$

within its stated parity-loop time, leaving all memory unchanged.

This implements the exact signs in subset-Moebius query evaluation.
explanation: This implements the exact signs in subset-Moebius query evaluation. Its memory-preserving contract applies to either sign of the supplied integer while charging the parity computation.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightSourceBucketOffsets.meets
theorem_title: Execution of bucket prefix offsets and initial cursors
natural_language_statement:
Let $c:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, $N,M\in\mathbb N$, and histogram, offset and cursor bases $a_h,a_o,a_c$ be given. Suppose the histogram in memory $\mu$ counts every code $c(i)<M$ for $i<N$, the regions satisfy $a_h+M\le a_o$ and $a_o+M+1\le a_c$, and $a_c+M$ fits memory. Let $\lambda,P,d$ be limits, program and depth with the offset body present, addresses fitting words and $N$ fitting a word. The routine writes

$$\nu(a_o+r)=\operatorname{offset}(c,N,r)\ (r\le M),\qquad\nu(a_c+r)=\operatorname{offset}(c,N,r)\ (r<M),$$

within its specified $M$-dependent time, changing no cell outside $[a_o,a_c+M)$.

This constructs exact contiguous bucket boundaries from actual histogram counts.
explanation: This constructs exact contiguous bucket boundaries from actual histogram counts. The stored prefix sums initialize both immutable offsets and mutable scatter cursors for every residue.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightSourceBucketScatter.meets
theorem_title: Execution of stable original-index bucket scattering
natural_language_statement:
Let $c:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ have $c(i)<M$ for $i<N$, with key, cursor and flat-index bases $a_k,a_c,a_f$. Suppose memory $\mu$ stores all keys and the initial prefix offsets at the cursors. Assume $a_k+N\le a_c$, $a_c+M\le a_f$, $a_f+N$ fits memory, and addresses fit words. In any Light program containing the scatter body, at depth $d$ it writes

$$\nu(a_f+\operatorname{position}(c,N,i))=i\quad(i<N),\qquad\nu(a_c+r)=\operatorname{offset}(c,N,r+1)\quad(r<M),$$

within its specified $N$-dependent time, preserving memory outside $[a_c,a_f+N)$.

This retains every physical input incidence exactly in its own residue bucket.
explanation: This retains every physical input incidence exactly in its own residue bucket. The final cursors equal the next bucket boundaries, and each index is written at its exact stable position.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightSourceRowScan.meets
theorem_title: Execution of endpoint cardinality and paired one-hot hashes
natural_language_statement:
Let $L,U\in\mathbb N$, bit map $s$ and nonnegative weight maps $w_0,w_1$ be given, with $s_i\le1$ and both weights at most $U$ for $i<L$. Suppose their three length-$L$ arrays are stored in memory $\mu$, all those arrays and a three-cell destination $b$ fit memory, addresses fit words and the explicit row-scan word budget fits. For limits, program and depth $\lambda,P,d$ with the scan body present, the procedure writes the cardinality $\sum_{i<L}s_i$ and the two complementary one-hot hash sums at $b,b+1,b+2$. It meets its specified linear scan time and changes no other cell.

This computes the literal endpoint statistics used for independent trimming and modular source encoding.
explanation: This computes the literal endpoint statistics used for independent trimming and modular source encoding.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightSubsetOffset.meets
theorem_title: Execution of a compact layer offset
natural_language_statement:
Let $W,L,k\in\mathbb N$ with $L,k\le W$, $a$ a correct Pascal-table base in memory $\mu$, and $\lambda,P,d$ limits, program and depth. Suppose the table fits memory, addresses fit words, $(W+1)2^{W+1}$ fits a word and the offset body is present. The procedure returns

$$\operatorname{layerOffset}(L,k)=\sum_{j<k}\binom Lj$$

within its specified $k$-dependent budget, leaving all memory unchanged.

This supplies the preceding-layer displacement for exact compact subset addresses.
explanation: This supplies the preceding-layer displacement for exact compact subset addresses. The finite sum of earlier binomial layers provides the displacement that precedes the current layer rank.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightWantedRow.meets
theorem_title: Appending a physical wanted-pair row
natural_language_statement:
Let $\ell,s,a,n,b,q\in\mathbb N$ denote a left index, right-index source base and start, row length, output base and previously emitted pair count. Let $\lambda,P,d,\mu$ be limits, program, depth and memory with the row body present. Suppose addresses fit words, the source slice ends before $b$, the pair output through $q+n$ fits memory, $\ell$ fits a word and all source values in the slice fit words. The procedure writes

$$\nu(b+2(q+t))=\ell,\qquad\nu(b+2(q+t)+1)=\mu(s+a+t)\quad(t<n),$$

within its specified $n$-dependent time, changing only the newly appended $2n$ cells.

This emits the exact physical matching-pair list without losing repeated original positions.
explanation: This emits the exact physical matching-pair list without losing repeated original positions. Each emitted pair keeps its left physical index and the corresponding retained right physical index.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LocalCoverMatrix.entry_eq_one_iff
theorem_title: Constructed support-matrix entries equal retained coverage
natural_language_statement:
Let $h,L,k,B\in\mathbb N$, $p=p(h)$ the local prime and $w$ a length-$L$ weight over its local field. For residues $a,b<p$, the actual histogram-trimmed matrix entry satisfies

$$\operatorname{entry}(w,k,B,ap+b)=1\iff\operatorname{Covers}(L,k,B,w,(a,b)).$$

This joins the literal Boolean support table to the finite-moment and greedy cover semantics.
explanation: This joins the literal Boolean support table to the finite-moment and greedy cover semantics. The equivalence identifies both independent bucket-cap conditions and the disjointness test with the cover predicate.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.ReportingHostFrontier.mem_frontier_iff
theorem_title: Exact raw-incidence membership of the actual frontier
natural_language_statement:
Let $h,J,k\in\mathbb N$ with $k\le J$, $I$ a finite raw-incidence set over finite decidable index types, $w$ a wanted label and $u$ a length-variable local-subset prefix. Then

$$u\in\operatorname{frontier}(I,w,k)\iff\exists r\in I:\ \operatorname{wantedOf}(r)=w\ \wedge\ \operatorname{take}_k(\operatorname{word}(r))=u.$$

This states completeness and exact membership of the executed reporting frontier in original raw incidences.
explanation: This states completeness and exact membership of the executed reporting frontier in original raw incidences.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SharedReportingBankCosts.host_time_le
theorem_title: Shared-bank host time fits the size-only budget
natural_language_statement:
Let $N_B,N_C,n\in\mathbb N$ with $N_B,N_C\le n$. Specialize the shared-host microblock parameter, block count and band size to the schedule at $n$. Then

$$T_{\mathrm{sharedHost}}(h(n),J(n),N_B,N_C,g(n))\le\operatorname{budget}_{\mathrm{sharedBank}}(n).$$

This gives a uniform original-input-size bound for reusable shared reporting preprocessing.
explanation: This gives a uniform original-input-size bound for reusable shared reporting preprocessing. Its assumptions bound the two actual normalized array lengths by the original input length before specializing the schedule.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SharedReportingBankResourceBounds.offset_le
theorem_title: Total shared-level offset is bounded by the cell envelope
natural_language_statement:
For every $h,J\in\mathbb N$, write $K(J)$ for the number of prescribed reporting levels and $C(h,J)$ for the uniform per-level cell bound. The packed level offset satisfies

$$\operatorname{offset}(h,J,K(J))\le K(J)C(h,J).$$

This converts the actual variable-size catalog packing into a finite total storage bound.
explanation: This converts the actual variable-size catalog packing into a finite total storage bound. It bounds the sum of the packed level extents by the number of levels times one uniform per-level reservation.
